name: Toshi Ichiyanagi
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; studied at Juilliard (1954-1957) and the New School with John Cage (from 1958), but first notable compositions (Kaiki, Distance) came after age 26 in 1960-1961.
early_history_summary: Born in Kobe to classically trained musician parents (cellist father, pianist mother). Began piano under mother's tutelage. By age 20, worked as a pianist at an American military base in Tokyo. Went to the US in 1952, studying at the University of Minnesota and Tanglewood with Aaron Copland, then Juilliard (1954-1957) and the New School with John Cage (from 1958).
family_context_summary: Born to a cellist father and pianist mother in Kobe; grew up in a musically rich household, though the family suffered during WWII when Western music was forbidden in Japan.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents were classically trained musicians, providing direct domain exposure and early piano training from his mother.
evidence_summary: Ichiyanagi benefited from a musical family background and early training, but his formative educational experiences at Juilliard and with Cage were not material milestones. His first notable compositions (Kaiki in 1960, Distance in 1961) came after age 26. Fame arrived later with his avant-garde works and co-founding of the Orchestral Space festival in 1966.

name: Christos Papadimitriou

name: Coxsone Dodd
milestone_by_age_26: Established the Sir Coxsone's Downbeat sound system in Kingston circa 1954, becoming one of Jamaica's top sound system operators and a foundational figure in the development of ska and reggae.
early_history_summary: Born in Kingston, Jamaica to a building contractor father who worked on the docks and a mother who ran a cold supper shop and liquor store where jazz records were played. As a teenager, developed a passion for jazz and R&B. Traveled to the American South as a seasonal farm laborer, where he amassed a collection of R&B records. Brought them back to Jamaica and launched his sound system around 1952-1954, quickly becoming a dominant operator in Kingston's competitive dancehall scene.
family_context_summary: Father Benjamin Dodd was a building contractor and dock worker who brought home jazz records from ships; mother Doris Darlington ran a cold supper shop and liquor store in Kingston where records were played for customers.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father's dock work provided access to imported records from visiting ships; mother's shop served as an early venue for playing music to customers, giving Dodd direct exposure to audience preferences.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Kingston sound system culture, family business platform, R&B record sourcing, dancehall direct exposure
evidence_summary: Dodd grew up immersed in Kingston's music scene through his family's businesses. His father's dock work and mother's shop provided early access to imported records and direct audience feedback. Kingston in the 1950s was the global frontier of sound system culture, and Dodd's position at its center gave him unmatched distribution and domain proximity. His rivalry with Duke Reid and innate musical ear drove him to become the dominant sound system operator, laying the groundwork for Studio One and the entire Jamaican recording industry.
starting_point: Born in Kingston, Jamaica to a building contractor father who worked on the docks and a mother who ran a cold supper shop and liquor store where jazz records were played for customers.
current_position: Died on May 4, 2004 at age 72 in Kingston; final role: founder and operator of Studio One, Jamaica's first Black-owned recording studio and the foundational label of ska, rocksteady, and reggae.

trajectory.event: Established the Sir Coxsone's Downbeat sound system in Kingston, becoming one of the island's top sound system operators.
Opened Studio One at 13 Brentford Road, Jamaica's first Black-owned recording studio.
Recorded Bob Marley and the Wailers; 'Simmer Down' topped the Jamaican charts for two months.
Formed the Skatalites as the house band, cementing Studio One's role in defining ska music.
Honored with street renaming of Brentford Road to Studio One Boulevard; died on May 4, 2004 in Kingston.

name: Horacio Accavallo
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; turned professional in 1956 (age 22) and fought in Italy 1958-59, but won no title or championship by age 26. World flyweight championship came in 1966 at age 31.
early_history_summary: Born in Villa Diamante, Lanús, Buenos Aires to illiterate Italian and Spanish immigrant parents. Grew up in extreme poverty in a shantytown, surviving by collecting cardboard and working as a shoeshine boy. Worked in a circus from ages 9-17 as a trapeze artist and performer. Started amateur boxing at age 14 and turned professional in 1956.
family_context_summary: Son of illiterate Italian (Roque) and Spanish (Balbina) immigrants; grew up in extreme poverty in a Buenos Aires shantytown, collecting cardboard and shining shoes to survive.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; parents were illiterate and had no connection to boxing.
evidence_summary: Accavallo's early career was defined by extreme poverty and a late start in boxing. While he was an active professional boxer by age 22 and fought in Italy by 1958-59, he had not won any title or championship by age 26. His defining achievement, the WBA/WBC world flyweight championship, came in 1966 at age 31. His story is one of adversity-driven self-creation rather than early advantage.

name: Giancarlo Fisichella
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Italian Formula Three Championship in 1994 with 10 race victories, including the prestigious Monaco F3 Grand Prix, establishing himself as a top single-seater prospect.
early_history_summary: Born in Rome to a noble Sicilian family; father owned a car garage and was a passionate F1 fan who introduced Giancarlo to karting at age 8 at the Guidonia circuit. Won the Italian Mini-Kart 60 Championship in 1984 with 12 victories. Progressed to Italian Formula Three in 1992, finishing 8th, then 2nd in 1993, before winning the championship in 1994 with RC Motorsport. Spent 1995-96 in DTM/ITC with Alfa Romeo before making his F1 debut with Minardi in 1996.
family_context_summary: Born to the noble Fisichella family of Sicily; father owned a car garage in Rome and was a passionate Formula One fan who took Giancarlo to kart tracks from age 8.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father's garage and F1 fandom provided direct mechanical and sporting domain exposure; father personally maintained Giancarlo's early kart before a professional mechanic was hired.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father's garage, F1 fandom, early karting, Italian F3 pipeline, motorsport domain exposure
evidence_summary: Fisichella's father, a garage owner and F1 enthusiast, provided direct domain exposure and practical support from age 8, maintaining his kart and fostering his racing passion. Over a decade of karting experience (1984-1991) built exceptional prior reps before his single-seater career. The Italian F3 championship served as a known F1 pipeline, and his 1994 title with 10 wins plus the Monaco F3 GP victory marked him as a top prospect. Italy's status as a motorsport hub provided a supportive ecosystem.
starting_point: Born in Rome to the noble Fisichella family of Sicily; father owned a car garage and was a passionate Formula One fan who introduced Giancarlo to karting at age 8.
current_position: Former Formula One driver (1996-2009) with 3 Grand Prix wins and 19 podiums across 229 starts; currently a Ferrari factory GT driver competing in WEC and IMSA; resides in Italy.

trajectory.event: Won the Italian Mini-Kart 60 Championship with 12 victories, launching a competitive karting career.
Won the Italian Formula Three Championship with 10 race victories including the Monaco F3 Grand Prix.
Made Formula One debut with Minardi at the Australian Grand Prix.
Achieved maiden F1 podium finishes at the Canadian and Belgian Grands Prix driving for Jordan.
Scored his first Formula One victory at the Brazilian Grand Prix driving for Jordan.
Drove for Ferrari after Felipe Massa's injury; transitioned to GT racing with AF Corse.
Won the 24 Hours of Le Mans with AF Corse alongside Gianmaria Bruni and Toni Vilander.

name: George Smith
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; received BA from Haverford College in 1963 (age 22) and was a graduate student at Harvard by age 26. PhD came in 1970 (age 29) and Nobel-winning phage display work in 1985 (age 44).

Pursued graduate work in molecular immunology under Edgar Haber at Massachusetts General Hospital, receiving PhD from Harvard in 1970. His Nobel Prize-winning phage display technology was developed during a sabbatical at Duke University in 1983-84.
family_context_summary: Born to Albert Mark Smith II and Jessie Patton Biggs Smith; father was born in 1908, mother in 1909. Family background not extensively documented beyond parental dates.
evidence_summary: Smith attended elite educational institutions (Phillips Academy Andover, Haverford College, Harvard) but had no material independently verifiable milestone by age 26. His college senior research project in 1962-63 initiated his engagement with molecular immunology, but his Nobel-winning phage display work was not published until 1985, when he was 44. His career is a case study in gradual scientific advancement rather than early breakthrough.

name: Klaus Hasselmann
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; received Diplom in physics from University of Hamburg in 1955 (age 24) and PhD from University of Göttingen in 1957 (age 26). These are educational achievements; major scientific contributions (stochastic climate model, Nobel Prize) came decades later.
early_history_summary: Born in Hamburg, Germany; family fled to England in 1934 due to the Nazi regime. Grew up in Welwyn Garden City, England, and received the Cambridge Higher School Certificate in 1949. Returned to Hamburg in 1949, did an internship in mechanical engineering, then studied physics and mathematics at the University of Hamburg, completing his Diplom in 1955. Pursued PhD at the University of Göttingen and the Max Planck Institute for Fluid Dynamics Research, completing it in 1957.
family_context_summary: Born in Hamburg; family emigrated to England in 1934 to escape the Nazi regime. Grew up in Welwyn Garden City, England, in a bilingual German-English environment.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond the family's emigration due to political circumstances.
evidence_summary: Hasselmann's early career consisted of standard educational milestones: a Diplom in physics (1955) and a PhD from Göttingen (1957), both completed by age 26. His major scientific contributions, including the stochastic climate model (1976) and climate change detection methods (1979), came decades later. He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2021 at age 90. No material independently verifiable career milestone occurred by age 26.

name: Jan Kaplický
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; received Diploma in Architecture from VSUP Prague in 1962 (age 25) and worked in private practice in Czechoslovakia 1964-68. Major works (Future Systems, Selfridges, Lord's Media Centre) came decades later.
early_history_summary: Born in Prague, the only child of a sculptor/painter father and a botanical illustrator mother. Grew up in the Ořechovka neighborhood of Prague under Nazi occupation. Studied architecture at the College of Applied Arts and Design (VSUP) in Prague from 1956-1962, receiving his Diploma in Architecture. Worked in private practice in Czechoslovakia from 1964-1968 before fleeing to London after the Soviet invasion.
family_context_summary: Only child of a sculptor and painter father and a botanical illustrator mother; grew up in an artistic household in Prague's Ořechovka neighborhood. Father's work as a sculptor exposed him to visual arts from an early age.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a sculptor and painter, mother was a botanical illustrator; both provided an artistic environment that influenced his design sensibility. Life magazine images inspired his passion for design.
evidence_summary: Kaplický grew up in an artistic family in Prague and completed his architecture diploma by age 25. By 26, he was in the early stages of private practice in Czechoslovakia with no notable built work. His career-defining achievements came much later: founding Future Systems in 1979, winning the RIBA Stirling Prize for the Lord's Media Centre in 1999, and completing the Selfridges Building in Birmingham in 2003. He fled to London in 1968 at age 31, which catalyzed his career.

name: Emilio Palma
milestone_by_age_26: No material personal milestone by age 26; fame derives entirely from the circumstance of being born at Argentina's Esperanza Base in Antarctica on January 7, 1978, which is not a personal achievement.
early_history_summary: Born at Fortín Sargento Cabral at the Esperanza Base on the Antarctic Peninsula. His father, Captain Jorge Emilio Palma, was head of the Argentine Army detachment at the base. His mother, Silvia Morella de Palma, was airlifted to the base while seven months pregnant to ensure the birth occurred on the Antarctic continent. The birth was part of Argentina's geopolitical strategy to assert territorial claims in Antarctica.
family_context_summary: Father was Captain Jorge Emilio Palma, head of the Argentine Army detachment at Esperanza Base; mother was Silvia Morella de Palma, who was airlifted to the base while pregnant.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father's military position directly enabled the circumstances of Emilio's birth at the Antarctic base; the birth was part of Argentina's geopolitical strategy.
evidence_summary: Palma's notability is entirely derived from the circumstance of his birth at an Argentine military base in Antarctica, engineered by his father's military assignment and Argentina's territorial claims strategy. This is not a personal achievement or milestone. He is featured in the Guinness Book of Records but has no documented personal accomplishments by age 26 or beyond.

name: Robert Lewandowski
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 2009-10 Ekstraklasa title with Lech Poznań as the league's top scorer with 18 goals, having previously been top scorer in all three of Poland's top divisions.
early_history_summary: Born in Warsaw to a sporting but modest family; father Krzysztof practiced judo and football, mother played volleyball. Began playing football at age 5 with Partyzant Leszno, then spent 7 years at UKS Varsovia Warsaw (1997-2004). Released by Legia Warsaw's reserve team around 2006 after his father's death. Joined third-tier Znicz Pruszków, where he was top scorer in the third division (2006-07) and second division (2007-08). Signed for Lech Poznań in 2008, winning the Polish Cup in 2009 and the Ekstraklasa title in 2010 as top scorer.
family_context_summary: Born in Warsaw to a sporting but modest family; father Krzysztof practiced judo and football and took Robert to a youth club in Warsaw at age 8. Mother and sister played volleyball. Father died of illness when Robert was 16, creating significant hardship.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a sports enthusiast who practiced judo and football; he took Robert to Varsovia Warsaw youth club at age 8 and fostered his early football development. No direct professional football connection in the family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father's death, release from Legia, lower-tier persistence, sporting family, youth coaching
evidence_summary: Lewandowski's path to elite football was marked by significant adversity: his father died when he was 16, and he was released by Legia Warsaw's reserves as a skinny teenager. He clawed his way up through Poland's third and second divisions as top scorer, earning a move to Lech Poznań where he won the Ekstraklasa at 21. His father's early sporting influence and introduction to Varsovia Warsaw provided foundational reps, but the driving force was constraint-driven self-creation through relentless goalscoring at every level. No significant financial platform or inherited network was documented.
starting_point: Born in Warsaw, Poland to a sporting but modest family; father Krzysztof was a judo and football enthusiast who worked various jobs, mother played volleyball; grew up in the small town of Leszno near Warsaw.
current_position: One of the greatest strikers in football history with 700+ senior career goals; plays for Chicago Fire in MLS and captains the Poland national team; estimated net worth approximately $100M.

trajectory.event: Finished as top scorer in Poland's third division with Znicz Pruszków, earning a promotion to the second tier.
Won the Ekstraklasa title with Lech Poznań as league top scorer with 18 goals; transferred to Borussia Dortmund.
Won his first Bundesliga title with Borussia Dortmund under manager Jürgen Klopp.
Scored four goals against Real Madrid in the Champions League semi-final; played in the final at Wembley.
Joined Bayern Munich on a free transfer from Borussia Dortmund.
Won the treble (Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal, Champions League) with Bayern Munich; named FIFA Best Men's Player.
Transferred to Barcelona; won La Liga title and Pichichi Trophy as top scorer in his first season.

name: Norm Macdonald
